26. // EventHandler enqueues reconcile.Requests in response to events (e.g. Pod Create).  EventHandlers map an Event
27. // for one object to trigger Reconciles for either the same object or different objects - e.g. if there is an
28. // Event for object with type Foo (using source.KindSource) then reconcile one or more object(s) with type Bar.
29. //
30. // Identical reconcile.Requests will be batched together through the queuing mechanism before reconcile is called.
31. //
32. // * Use EnqueueRequestForObject to reconcile the object the event is for
33. // - do this for events for the type the Controller Reconciles. (e.g. Deployment for a Deployment Controller)

35. // * Use EnqueueRequestForOwner to reconcile the owner of the object the event is for
36. // - do this for events for the types the Controller creates.  (e.g. ReplicaSets created by a Deployment Controller)

38. // * Use EnqueueRequestsFromMapFunc to transform an event for an object to a reconcile of an object
39. // of a different type - do this for events for types the Controller may be interested in, but doesn't create.

42. func TestDynamicEnqueueRequest_AddHandler(t *testing.T) {
43. 	tests := []struct {
44. 		name               string
45. 		args               HandlerRegistration
46. 		wantErr            bool
47. 		registeredHandlers int
48. 	}{
49. 		{
50. 			name:               "registers the given handler with no error",
51. 			args:               &fakeHandler{},
52. 			wantErr:            false,
53. 			registeredHandlers: 1,
54. 		},
55. 	}
56. 	for _, tt := range tests {
57. 		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
58. 			d := NewDynamicEnqueueRequest()
59. 			if err := d.AddHandler(tt.args); (err != nil) != tt.wantErr {
60. 				t.Errorf("DynamicEnqueueRequest.AddHandler() error = %v, wantErr %v", err, tt.wantErr)
61. 			}
62. 			assert.Equal(t, len(d.registrations), tt.registeredHandlers)
63. 		})
64. 	}
65. }

67. func TestDynamicEnqueueRequest_RemoveHandler(t *testing.T) {
68. 	tests := []struct {
69. 		name               string
70. 		setup              func(handler *DynamicEnqueueRequest)
71. 		args               HandlerRegistration
72. 		registeredHandlers int
73. 	}{
74. 		{
75. 			name: "removal on empty handler is a NOOP",
76. 			args: &fakeHandler{},
77. 		},
78. 		{
79. 			name: "succeed on initialized handler",
80. 			args: &fakeHandler{},
81. 			setup: func(handler *DynamicEnqueueRequest) {

83. 				assert.Equal(t, len(handler.registrations), 1)
84. 			},
85. 			registeredHandlers: 0,
86. 		},
87. 		{
88. 			name: "uses key to identify transformer",
89. 			args: &fakeHandler{
90. 				name: "bar",
91. 			},
92. 			setup: func(handler *DynamicEnqueueRequest) {
93. 				assert.NoError(t, handler.AddHandler(&fakeHandler{
94. 					name: "foo",
95. 				}))
96. 				assert.Equal(t, len(handler.registrations), 1)
97. 			},
98. 			registeredHandlers: 1,
99. 		},
100. 	}

105. 				tt.setup(d)

113. func TestDynamicEnqueueRequest_EventHandler(t *testing.T) {
114. 	// Fixtures
115. 	nsn1 := types.NamespacedName{
116. 		Namespace: "default",
117. 		Name:      "watched1",
118. 	}
119. 	testObject1 := &corev1.Secret{
120. 		ObjectMeta: k8s.ToObjectMeta(nsn1),
121. 	}
122. 	updated1 := testObject1
123. 	updated1.Labels = map[string]string{"updated": "1"}
124. 
125. 	nsn2 := types.NamespacedName{
126. 		Namespace: "default",
127. 		Name:      "watched2",
128. 	}
129. 	testObject2 := &corev1.Secret{
130. 		ObjectMeta: k8s.ToObjectMeta(nsn2),
131. 	}
132. 	updated2 := testObject2
133. 	updated2.Labels = map[string]string{"updated": "2"}
134. 
135. 	watching := types.NamespacedName{
136. 		Namespace: "default",
137. 		Name:      "watcher",
138. 	}
139. 
140. 	d := NewDynamicEnqueueRequest()
141. 	require.NoError(t, d.InjectMapper(getRESTMapper()))
142. 	q := workqueue.NewRateLimitingQueue(workqueue.DefaultControllerRateLimiter())
143. 
144. 	assertEmptyQueue := func() {
145. 		require.Equal(t, 0, q.Len())
146. 	}
147. 	getReconcileReqFromQueue := func() reconcile.Request {
148. 		item, shutdown := q.Get()
149. 		defer q.Done(item)
150. 		require.False(t, shutdown)
151. 		req, ok := item.(reconcile.Request)
152. 		require.True(t, ok)
153. 		return req
154. 	}
155. 	assertReconcileReq := func(nsn types.NamespacedName) {
156. 		require.Equal(t, getReconcileReqFromQueue().NamespacedName, nsn)
157. 	}
158. 
159. 	assertEmptyQueue()
160. 
161. 	// simulate an object creation
162. 	d.Create(event.CreateEvent{
163. 		Object: testObject1,
164. 	}, q)
165. 	assertEmptyQueue()
166. 
167. 	// Add a watch for the first object
168. 	require.NoError(t, d.AddHandler(NamedWatch{
169. 		Watched: []types.NamespacedName{nsn1},
170. 		Watcher: watching,
171. 		Name:    "test-watch-1",
172. 	}))
173. 	assertEmptyQueue()
174. 
175. 	// simulate first object creation
176. 	d.Create(event.CreateEvent{
177. 		Object: testObject1,
178. 	}, q)
179. 	assertReconcileReq(watching)
180. 
181. 	// simulate object update
182. 	d.Update(event.UpdateEvent{
183. 		ObjectOld: testObject1,
184. 		ObjectNew: updated1,
185. 	}, q)
186. 	assertReconcileReq(watching)
187. 	// simulate object deletion
188. 	d.Delete(event.DeleteEvent{
189. 		Object: testObject1,
190. 	}, q)
191. 	assertReconcileReq(watching)
192. 
193. 	// simulate second object creation
194. 	d.Create(event.CreateEvent{
195. 		Object: testObject2,
196. 	}, q)
197. 	// no watcher, nothing in the queue
198. 	assertEmptyQueue()
199. 	// simulate second object update
200. 	d.Update(event.UpdateEvent{
201. 		ObjectOld: testObject2,
202. 		ObjectNew: updated2,
203. 	}, q)
204. 	// no watcher, nothing in the queue
205. 	assertEmptyQueue()
206. 
207. 	// register a second watch for the second object
208. 	require.NoError(t, d.AddHandler(NamedWatch{
209. 		Watched: []types.NamespacedName{nsn2},
210. 		Watcher: watching,
211. 		Name:    "test-watch-2",
212. 	}))
213. 	// simulate second object creation
214. 	d.Create(event.CreateEvent{
215. 		Object: testObject2,
216. 	}, q)
217. 	assertReconcileReq(watching)
218. 	// simulate second object update
219. 	d.Update(event.UpdateEvent{
220. 		ObjectOld: testObject2,

220. 		ObjectOld: testObject2,
221. 		ObjectNew: updated2,
222. 	}, q)
223. 	assertReconcileReq(watching)
224. 
225. 	// remove the watch for object 2
226. 	d.RemoveHandlerForKey("test-watch-2")
227. 	// simulate object update: nothing should happen
228. 	d.Update(event.UpdateEvent{
229. 		ObjectOld: testObject2,
230. 		ObjectNew: updated2,
231. 	}, q)
232. 	assertEmptyQueue()
233. 
234. 	// updates on the first object should still work
235. 	d.Update(event.UpdateEvent{
236. 		ObjectOld: testObject1,
237. 		ObjectNew: updated1,
238. 	}, q)
239. 	assertReconcileReq(watching)
240. 
241. 	// let's combine both objects in a single watch
242. 	require.NoError(t, d.AddHandler(NamedWatch{
243. 		Name:    "test-watch-1",
244. 		Watched: []types.NamespacedName{nsn1, nsn2},
245. 		Watcher: watching,
246. 	}))
247. 
248. 	// update on the first object should register
249. 	d.Update(event.UpdateEvent{
250. 		ObjectOld: testObject1,
251. 		ObjectNew: updated1,
252. 	}, q)
253. 	assertReconcileReq(watching)
254. 
255. 	// update on the second object should register too
256. 	d.Update(event.UpdateEvent{
257. 		ObjectOld: testObject2,
258. 		ObjectNew: updated2,
259. 	}, q)
260. 	assertReconcileReq(watching)
261. 
262. 	// going back to watching object 1 only
263. 	require.NoError(t, d.AddHandler(NamedWatch{
264. 		Watched: []types.NamespacedName{nsn1},
265. 		Watcher: watching,
266. 		Name:    "test-watch-1",
267. 	}))
268. 	assertEmptyQueue()
269. 
270. 	// setup an owner watch where owner is testObject1
271. 	require.NoError(t, d.AddHandler(&OwnerWatch{
272. 		EnqueueRequestForOwner: handler.EnqueueRequestForOwner{
273. 			OwnerType:    testObject1,
274. 			IsController: true,
275. 		},
276. 	}))
277. 
278. 	// let's make object 1 the owner of object 2
279. 	require.NoError(t, controllerutil.SetControllerReference(testObject1, testObject2, scheme.Scheme))
280. 	// an update on object 2 should enqueue a request for object 1 (the owner)
281. 	d.Update(event.UpdateEvent{
282. 		ObjectOld: testObject2,
283. 		ObjectNew: updated2,
284. 	}, q)
285. 	assertReconcileReq(nsn1)
286. 	// same for deletes
287. 	d.Delete(event.DeleteEvent{
288. 		Object: testObject2,
289. 	}, q)
290. 	assertReconcileReq(nsn1)
291. 
292. 	// named watch on object 1 should still work
293. 	d.Create(event.CreateEvent{
294. 		Object: testObject1,
295. 	}, q)
296. 	assertReconcileReq(watching)
297. 
298. 	// it's possible to have both an owner watch and a named watch triggered
299. 	// for a single event
300. 	// add a named watch on object 2
301. 	require.NoError(t, d.AddHandler(NamedWatch{
302. 		Watched: []types.NamespacedName{nsn2},
303. 		Watcher: watching,
304. 		Name:    "test-watch-2",
305. 	}))
306. 	d.Create(event.CreateEvent{
307. 		Object: testObject2,
308. 	}, q)
309. 	expected := []types.NamespacedName{
310. 		// owner watch (for object1) should trigger since object2's owner is object1
311. 		nsn1,
312. 		// named watch (for object2) should trigger since object2 was updated
313. 		watching,
314. 	}
315. 	// actual order is non-deterministic
316. 	req1 := getReconcileReqFromQueue()
317. 	req2 := getReconcileReqFromQueue()
318. 	require.ElementsMatch(t, expected, []types.NamespacedName{req1.NamespacedName, req2.NamespacedName})
319. }

95. 		if !referenced || softOwner.Kind != policyv1alpha1.Kind {
96. 			return nil
97. 		}
98. 		return []reconcile.Request{

105. func (r *ReconcileStackConfigPolicy) reconcileRequestForAllPolicies() handler.EventHandler {
106. 	return handler.EnqueueRequestsFromMapFunc(func(es client.Object) []reconcile.Request {
107. 		var stackConfigList policyv1alpha1.StackConfigPolicyList
108. 		err := r.Client.List(context.Background(), &stackConfigList)
109. 		if err != nil {

116. 			requests = append(requests, reconcile.Request{NamespacedName: k8s.ExtractNamespacedName(&stackConfig)})
117. 		}
118. 		return requests
119. 	})
120. }

20. // WatchUserProvidedSecrets registers a watch for user-provided secrets that are in the same namespace as the watcher.
21. // Only one watch per watcher is registered:
22. // - if it already exists with different secrets, it is replaced to watch the new secrets.
23. // - if there is no secret provided by the user, remove the watch.
24. func WatchUserProvidedSecrets(
25. 	watcher types.NamespacedName, // resource to which the watches are attached (e.g. an Elasticsearch object)
26. 	watched DynamicWatches, // existing dynamic watches
27. 	watchName string, // dynamic watch to register
28. 	secrets []string, // user-provided secrets to watch
29. ) error {
30. 	secretSources := make([]commonv1.NamespacedSecretSource, 0, len(secrets))
31. 	for _, secretName := range secrets {
32. 		secretSources = append(secretSources, commonv1.NamespacedSecretSource{Namespace: watcher.Namespace, SecretName: secretName})
33. 	}
34. 	return WatchUserProvidedNamespacedSecrets(watcher, watched, watchName, secretSources)
35. }
36. 
37. // WatchUserProvidedNamespacedSecrets registers a watch for user-provided secrets that are in any namespace.
38. // Only one watch per watcher is registered:
39. // - if it already exists with different secrets, it is replaced to watch the new secrets.
40. // - if there is no secret provided by the user, remove the watch.
41. func WatchUserProvidedNamespacedSecrets(
42. 	watcher types.NamespacedName, // resource to which the watches are attached (e.g. an Elasticsearch object)
43. 	watched DynamicWatches, // existing dynamic watches
44. 	watchName string, // dynamic watch to register
45. 	secrets []commonv1.NamespacedSecretSource, // secrets to watch
46. ) error {
47. 	if len(secrets) == 0 {
48. 		watched.Secrets.RemoveHandlerForKey(watchName)
49. 		return nil
50. 	}
51. 	userSecretNsns := make([]types.NamespacedName, 0, len(secrets))
52. 	for _, s := range secrets {
53. 		userSecretNsns = append(userSecretNsns, types.NamespacedName{
54. 			Namespace: s.Namespace,
55. 			Name:      s.SecretName,
56. 		})
57. 	}
58. 	return watched.Secrets.AddHandler(NamedWatch{
59. 		Name:    watchName,
60. 		Watched: userSecretNsns,
61. 		Watcher: watcher,
62. 	})
63. }

73. func reconcileReqForSoftOwner(kind string) handler.MapFunc {
74. 	return func(object client.Object) []reconcile.Request {
75. 		softOwner, referenced := reconciler.SoftOwnerRefFromLabels(object.GetLabels())
76. 		if !referenced {
77. 			return nil
78. 		}
79. 		if softOwner.Kind != kind {
80. 			return nil
81. 		}
82. 		return []reconcile.Request{
83. 			{NamespacedName: types.NamespacedName{Namespace: softOwner.Namespace, Name: softOwner.Name}},
84. 		}
85. 	}
86. }

26. // AddWatches set watches on objects needed to manage the association between a local and a remote cluster.
27. func AddWatches(c controller.Controller, r *ReconcileRemoteCa) error {
28. 	// Watch for changes to RemoteCluster
29. 	if err := c.Watch(&source.Kind{Type: &esv1.Elasticsearch{}}, &handler.EnqueueRequestForObject{}); err != nil {
30. 		return err
31. 	}
32. 
33. 	// Watch Secrets that contain remote certificate authorities managed by this controller
34. 	if err := c.Watch(&source.Kind{Type: &v1.Secret{}}, handler.EnqueueRequestsFromMapFunc(newRequestsFromMatchedLabels())); err != nil {
35. 		return err
36. 	}
37. 
38. 	// Dynamically watches the certificate authorities involved in a cluster relationship
39. 	if err := c.Watch(&source.Kind{Type: &v1.Secret{}}, r.watches.Secrets); err != nil {
40. 		return err
41. 	}
42. 
43. 	return r.watches.Secrets.AddHandlers(
44. 		&watches.OwnerWatch{
45. 			EnqueueRequestForOwner: handler.EnqueueRequestForOwner{
46. 				IsController: true,
47. 				OwnerType:    &esv1.Elasticsearch{},
48. 			},
49. 		},
50. 	)
51. }

53. // newRequestsFromMatchedLabels creates a watch handler function that creates reconcile requests based on the
54. // labels set on a Secret which contains the remote CA.
55. func newRequestsFromMatchedLabels() handler.MapFunc {
56. 	return func(obj client.Object) []reconcile.Request {
57. 		labels := obj.GetLabels()
58. 		if !maps.ContainsKeys(labels, RemoteClusterNameLabelName, RemoteClusterNamespaceLabelName, commonv1.TypeLabelName) {
59. 			return nil
60. 		}
61. 		if labels[commonv1.TypeLabelName] != remoteca.TypeLabelValue {
62. 			return nil
63. 		}
64. 		return []reconcile.Request{
65. 			{NamespacedName: types.NamespacedName{
66. 				Namespace: labels[RemoteClusterNamespaceLabelName],
67. 				Name:      labels[RemoteClusterNameLabelName]},
68. 			},
69. 		}
70. 	}
71. }

73. func watchName(local types.NamespacedName, remote types.NamespacedName) string {
74. 	return fmt.Sprintf(
75. 		"%s-%s-%s-%s",
76. 		local.Namespace,
77. 		local.Name,
78. 		remote.Namespace,
79. 		remote.Name,
80. 	)

17. // WatchPods updates the given controller to enqueue reconciliation requests triggered by changes on Pods.
18. // The resource to reconcile is identified by a label on the Pods.
19. func WatchPods(c controller.Controller, objNameLabel string) error {
20. 	return c.Watch(
21. 		&source.Kind{Type: &corev1.Pod{}},
22. 		handler.EnqueueRequestsFromMapFunc(objToReconcileRequest(objNameLabel)),
23. 	)
24. }
25. 
26. // objToReconcileRequest returns a function to enqueue reconcile requests for the resource name set at objNameLabel.
27. func objToReconcileRequest(objNameLabel string) func(object client.Object) []reconcile.Request {
28. 	return func(object client.Object) []reconcile.Request {
29. 		labels := object.GetLabels()
30. 		objectName, isSet := labels[objNameLabel]
31. 		if !isSet {
32. 			return nil
33. 		}
34. 		return []reconcile.Request{
35. 			{
36. 				NamespacedName: types.NamespacedName{
37. 					Namespace: object.GetNamespace(),
38. 					Name:      objectName,
39. 				},
40. 			},
41. 		}
42. 	}
43. }

17. // WatchPods updates the given controller to enqueue reconciliation requests triggered by changes on Pods.
18. // The resource to reconcile is identified by a label on the Pods.
19. func WatchPods(c controller.Controller, objNameLabel string) error {
20. 	return c.Watch(
21. 		&source.Kind{Type: &corev1.Pod{}},
22. 		handler.EnqueueRequestsFromMapFunc(objToReconcileRequest(objNameLabel)),
23. 	)
24. }
25. 
26. // objToReconcileRequest returns a function to enqueue reconcile requests for the resource name set at objNameLabel.
27. func objToReconcileRequest(objNameLabel string) func(object client.Object) []reconcile.Request {
28. 	return func(object client.Object) []reconcile.Request {
29. 		labels := object.GetLabels()
30. 		objectName, isSet := labels[objNameLabel]
31. 		if !isSet {
32. 			return nil
33. 		}
34. 		return []reconcile.Request{
35. 			{
36. 				NamespacedName: types.NamespacedName{
37. 					Namespace: object.GetNamespace(),
38. 					Name:      objectName,
39. 				},
40. 			},
41. 		}
42. 	}
43. }

5. 	"errors"
6. 	"fmt"
7. 	"time"

12. 	"k8s.io/client-go/util/workqueue"
13. 	"sigs.k8s.io/controller-runtime/pkg/cache"
14. 	"sigs.k8s.io/controller-runtime/pkg/client"
15. 	"sigs.k8s.io/controller-runtime/pkg/handler"
16. 	"sigs.k8s.io/controller-runtime/pkg/predicate"
17. )
18. 
19. // Kind is used to provide a source of events originating inside the cluster from Watches (e.g. Pod Create).
20. type Kind struct {
21. 	// Type is the type of object to watch.  e.g. &v1.Pod{}
22. 	Type client.Object
23. 
24. 	// Cache used to watch APIs
25. 	Cache cache.Cache
26. 
27. 	// started may contain an error if one was encountered during startup. If its closed and does not
28. 	// contain an error, startup and syncing finished.
29. 	started     chan error
30. 	startCancel func()
31. }
32. 
33. // Start is internal and should be called only by the Controller to register an EventHandler with the Informer
34. // to enqueue reconcile.Requests.
35. func (ks *Kind) Start(ctx context.Context, handler handler.EventHandler, queue workqueue.RateLimitingInterface,
36. 	prct ...predicate.Predicate) error {
37. 	if ks.Type == nil {
38. 		return fmt.Errorf("must create Kind with a non-nil object")
39. 	}
40. 	if ks.Cache == nil {
41. 		return fmt.Errorf("must create Kind with a non-nil cache")
42. 	}
43. 
44. 	// cache.GetInformer will block until its context is cancelled if the cache was already started and it can not
45. 	// sync that informer (most commonly due to RBAC issues).
46. 	ctx, ks.startCancel = context.WithCancel(ctx)
47. 	ks.started = make(chan error)
48. 	go func() {
49. 		var (
50. 			i       cache.Informer
51. 			lastErr error
52. 		)
53. 
54. 		// Tries to get an informer until it returns true,
55. 		// an error or the specified context is cancelled or expired.
56. 		if err := wait.PollUntilContextCancel(ctx, 10*time.Second, true, func(ctx context.Context) (bool, error) {
57. 			// Lookup the Informer from the Cache and add an EventHandler which populates the Queue
58. 			i, lastErr = ks.Cache.GetInformer(ctx, ks.Type)
59. 			if lastErr != nil {
60. 				kindMatchErr := &meta.NoKindMatchError{}
61. 				switch {
62. 				case errors.As(lastErr, &kindMatchErr):
63. 					log.Error(lastErr, "if kind is a CRD, it should be installed before calling Start",
64. 						"kind", kindMatchErr.GroupKind)
65. 				case runtime.IsNotRegisteredError(lastErr):
66. 					log.Error(lastErr, "kind must be registered to the Scheme")
67. 				default:
68. 					log.Error(lastErr, "failed to get informer from cache")
69. 				}
70. 				return false, nil // Retry.
71. 			}
72. 			return true, nil
73. 		}); err != nil {
74. 			if lastErr != nil {
75. 				ks.started <- fmt.Errorf("failed to get informer from cache: %w", lastErr)
76. 				return
77. 			}
78. 			ks.started <- err
79. 			return
80. 		}
81. 
82. 		_, err := i.AddEventHandler(NewEventHandler(ctx, queue, handler, prct).HandlerFuncs())
83. 		if err != nil {
84. 			ks.started <- err
85. 			return
86. 		}
87. 		if !ks.Cache.WaitForCacheSync(ctx) {
88. 			// Would be great to return something more informative here
89. 			ks.started <- errors.New("cache did not sync")
90. 		}
91. 		close(ks.started)
92. 	}()
93. 
94. 	return nil
95. }
96. 
97. func (ks *Kind) String() string {
98. 	if ks.Type != nil {
99. 		return fmt.Sprintf("kind source: %T", ks.Type)
100. 	}
101. 	return "kind source: unknown type"
102. }
103. 
104. // WaitForSync implements SyncingSource to allow controllers to wait with starting
105. // workers until the cache is synced.
106. func (ks *Kind) WaitForSync(ctx context.Context) error {
107. 	select {
108. 	case err := <-ks.started:
109. 		return err
110. 	case <-ctx.Done():
111. 		ks.startCancel()
112. 		if errors.Is(ctx.Err(), context.Canceled) {
113. 			return nil
114. 		}
115. 		return fmt.Errorf("timed out waiting for cache to be synced for Kind %T", ks.Type)
116. 	}
117. }

43. func addWatches(c controller.Controller, r *Reconciler) error {
44. 	// Watch the associated resource (e.g. Kibana for a Kibana -> Elasticsearch association)

50. 	if err := c.Watch(&source.Kind{Type: &corev1.Secret{}}, &handler.EnqueueRequestForOwner{
51. 		OwnerType:    r.AssociatedObjTemplate(),
52. 		IsController: true,
53. 	}); err != nil {
54. 		return err
55. 	}
56. 
57. 	// Dynamically watch the referenced resources (e.g. Elasticsearch B for a Kibana A -> Elasticsearch B association)
58. 	if err := c.Watch(&source.Kind{Type: r.ReferencedObjTemplate()}, r.watches.ReferencedResources); err != nil {
59. 		return err
60. 	}
61. 
62. 	// Dynamically watch Secrets (CA Secret of the referenced resource, ES user secret or custom referenced object secret)
63. 	if err := c.Watch(&source.Kind{Type: &corev1.Secret{}}, r.watches.Secrets); err != nil {
64. 		return err
65. 	}
66. 
67. 	// Dynamically watch Service objects for custom services setup by the user
68. 	return c.Watch(&source.Kind{Type: &corev1.Service{}}, r.watches.Services)

51. func WithCustomValidator(scheme *runtime.Scheme, obj runtime.Object, validator CustomValidator) *Webhook {
52. 	return &Webhook{
53. 		Handler: &validatorForType{object: obj, validator: validator, decoder: NewDecoder(scheme)},
54. 	}
55. }

58. 	validator CustomValidator
59. 	object    runtime.Object
60. 	decoder   *Decoder
61. }

65. 	if h.decoder == nil {
66. 		panic("decoder should never be nil")
67. 	}
68. 	if h.validator == nil {
69. 		panic("validator should never be nil")
70. 	}
71. 	if h.object == nil {
72. 		panic("object should never be nil")
73. 	}
74. 
75. 	ctx = NewContextWithRequest(ctx, req)
76. 
77. 	// Get the object in the request
78. 	obj := h.object.DeepCopyObject()
79. 
80. 	var err error
81. 	var warnings []string
82. 
83. 	switch req.Operation {
84. 	case v1.Connect:
85. 		// No validation for connect requests.

99. 			return Errored(http.StatusBadRequest, err)
